zebralogic.title: Interpret adjacency and ordering clues correctly
zebralogic.principle: When a clue uses terms like 'directly left of', 'directly right of', 'next to', or similar, enforce that the two houses are adjacent in the specified order.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue mentions direct adjacency or ordering between two attributes.
zebralogic.example: Treating 'X is directly left of Y' as merely 'X is somewhere left of Y', allowing non‑adjacent placements.

zebralogic.title: Interpret distance clues correctly
zebralogic.principle: When a clue states 'N houses between X and Y', enforce that exactly N other houses separate X and Y, i.e., the distance between them is N+1.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue mentions a specific number of houses between two attributes.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting '2 houses between X and Y' as X and Y being two houses apart instead of three.

zebralogic.title: Treat 'somewhere left/right of' as inequality
zebralogic.principle: Interpret 'somewhere left of' or 'somewhere right of' as a strict ordering constraint (pos(X) < pos(Y) or pos(X) > pos(Y)), not requiring adjacency.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses 'somewhere left of' or 'somewhere right of' without 'directly'.
zebralogic.example: Treating 'X is somewhere left of Y' as 'X is directly left of Y', restricting placements unnecessarily.

zebralogic.title: Enforce uniqueness across each attribute category
zebralogic.principle: Each value in a category must appear exactly once across all houses; no two houses may share the same value.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: During assignment of any attribute, ensure the value hasn't been used elsewhere.
zebralogic.example: Assigning the hobby 'painting' to two different houses.

zebralogic.title: Preserve original case of attribute values
zebralogic.principle: Copy attribute values exactly as they appear in the problem statement, preserving spelling and case.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When constructing the final output JSON.

zebralogic.title: Bidirectional equivalence for name‑attribute clues
zebralogic.principle: If a clue links a specific name to an attribute, enforce both directions: the name has that attribute and the attribute belongs to that name.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue directly ties a name to a value (e.g., 'Arnold's birthday is January').
zebralogic.example: Setting Arnold's birthday to January but not preventing another person from also having January.

zebralogic.title: Bidirectional equivalence for attribute‑attribute clues
zebralogic.principle: When a clue states that two attributes belong to the same house, enforce the equivalence in both directions.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue links two non‑name attributes (e.g., 'doctor is baseball').
zebralogic.example: Setting the doctor to love baseball but allowing another house to also love baseball.

zebralogic.title: Apply direct placement constraints
zebralogic.principle: If a clue explicitly places an attribute in a specific house number, enforce that placement exactly.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a house index (e.g., 'Eric is in the fifth house').
zebralogic.example: Ignoring the clue and allowing Eric to be placed in house 3.

zebralogic.title: Output solution JSON with exact schema and no extra text
zebralogic.principle: Emit only the JSON object with the required top‑level keys and structure; any extra characters cause the verifier to reject the answer.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When finalizing the answer for a zebralogic problem.
zebralogic.example: Including a sentence like 'Here is the solution:' before the JSON.

zebralogic.title: Chain adjacency clues into consecutive blocks
zebralogic.principle: When multiple clues each state a direct left/right relationship that share an intermediate attribute, combine them to infer a longer consecutive sequence of houses in the specified order.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever you have two or more adjacency clues that connect a chain of attributes (e.g., X left of Y and Y left of Z).
zebralogic.example: Treating 'X left of Y' and 'Y left of Z' independently, allowing X and Z to be non‑adjacent, thus missing the requirement that X, Y, Z occupy three consecutive houses.

zebralogic.description: Interpreting 'N houses between' as distance N
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model reads the phrase as a direct distance rather than counting the houses that lie between the two.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: When a clue says 'N houses between X and Y', enforce that exactly N other houses separate X and Y, i.e., |pos(X) - pos(Y)| = N + 1.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring equivalence clues that bind two attributes to the same house
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model treats the clue as a one‑way implication and fails to enforce the reverse direction.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Apply bidirectional equivalence for any clue that links two attributes, ensuring both attributes are assigned to the same house.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model may assign the same value of an attribute category to multiple houses.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Maintain a set of used values for each category and prevent reuse.

zebralogic.description: Altering attribute values (spelling/casing) instead of copying them verbatim
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model normalizes or changes the case of strings during generation.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Copy attribute strings exactly as they appear in the problem statement.

zebralogic.description: Including extra explanatory text or stray characters outside the required JSON solution
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model adds commentary or formatting before/after the JSON, breaking the parser.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Output only the JSON object with the required keys, no surrounding text.
